evidence: Added branch (var_tmp): `elif [ "$var_tmp_cleanup" -lt 0 ]; then logger -t rebar-health "could NOT determine whether anything bounds ${VAR_TMP_DIR} — ${VARTMP_CAP_SH} did not answer; this is an unmeasured state, not a bound known to be absent; ..."`
Added branch (journald) and (container) are structurally identical new elif logger lines in the same diff
tests/scripts/test_observability_var_tmp.py:98: `_stub(bin_dir, "logger", "exit 0")` — logger output is discarded, and no test in the changed suites greps logger output

review-bot-ops.md added table documents `-1` -> 'the check could not be answered at all ... check that the script it resolves exists on the box', an operator-facing contract with no test asserting the message is emitted with the offending script name

Named triggering input: a cap script that `exit 127` (empty stdout, non-zero rc) — exactly the container/var_tmp table row `("exit 127", -1)` — reaches the metric-value assertion but not the log branch
advisory.finding: The three newly-added `-1`/UNKNOWN operator-diagnostic log branches in observability.sh (journald, var_tmp, container: `elif [ "$x" -lt 0 ]; then logger -t rebar-health "could NOT determine ..."`) are not exercised by any test. Every fixture stubs `logger` as `exit 0` and no test captures its output, so the distinct 'could NOT determine ... did not answer; this is an unmeasured state' message — which the runbook tells operators to read to distinguish an unmeasured cap from a cap known absent — could be deleted, mis-wired, or made to name the wrong script and every suite would still pass.
scenarios: A refactor renames the log branch's variable interpolation so it no longer names the failing script; operators still see a message but not the actionable path, and no test fails
The `-lt 0` branch is accidentally dropped, leaving `-1` published with no diagnostic line; the paging value test still passes
advisory.suggested_fix: In the var_tmp UNKNOWN table case (and a container equivalent), replace the discarding logger stub with one that appends `$*` to a log file and assert the captured line contains 'could NOT determine' and the cap-script path for the -1 rows.

ticket octahedral-auburn-sunfish (5246-2ec0-1fa6-4637): 'A commit that changes ONLY a cap value ... changes no path in any manifest, so autodeploy signals nothing and the new ceiling is not applied'
dropped.finding: install-observability.sh now deploys /usr/local/bin/docker-storage-cap.sh and /usr/local/bin/journald-cap.sh which the probe executes, but autodeploy's OBS_PATHS trigger does not include the cap scripts, so a change confined to a cap script does not re-run the installer and the installed copies drift from the checkout indefinitely.
scenarios: An operator edits a ceiling in journald-cap.sh or docker-storage-cap.sh (the ADR 0112 decision-6 edit) and commits it alone; autodeploy signals nothing, /usr/local/bin/journald-cap.sh stays at the old value, and the probe keeps measuring against a ceiling no longer in the tree.
